children: Ryanair's better pricing outlook for winter combined with a new buyback should give shares a lift despite the challenge of fuel prices, J.P. Morgan says in a research note. JPM expects the Irish airline group to raise fares by at least a mid-teen percentage to offset the additional 2 billion-euro fuel bill, but near-term pricing should soothe the market since it indicates that underlying demand is strong enough to allow Ryanair to at least partially offset the current outlook on forward pricing. Ryanair could get some additional pricing power into next year if other airlines need to reduce capacity further, the analysts say. (sarah.sloat@wsj.com)
